title: Independent cell decay lowered dedicated input counts in models of 13 of 655 selected Allen circuits
abstract: We tested whether intrinsic cell dynamics change the minimum dedicated input count in small models of Allen cortical slice circuits. The sample had 556 mouse VisP and 99 human TCx recordings with three to six selected excitatory cells. Exact input-subset tests included full matching and input accessibility. Independent free decay terms lowered the count in 13 of 655 graphs: by one in 12 and by two in one. A common scalar decay preserves the Kalman rank and cannot cause this change. Only 157 selected graphs had a detected edge; 498 were empty. A matching-only shortcut underestimated dedicated input counts in 18 graphs. Exact enumeration gave 721 states with fixed labeled degrees and tested-pair masks. Model costs varied across compatible graphs in four recordings per diagonal rule. Their difference varied in two. Checks on all three-cell graphs passed. These are structural model results, not measured neural control. Sparse selected slice graphs, independent parameter assumptions, omitted cells and uncertain connection calls limit transfer. Original code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and external retrieval steps support reproduction. External records are excluded.

display.caption: Minimum dedicated input counts under zero or common decay and independent cell decay in 655 selected Allen circuit models. The last panel compares decay sensitivity and matching-only underestimates. These are separate counts and can overlap.
